meta.session_title: Day 1 - Introduction to Java & Language Fundamentals
meta.pedagogy: Hands-on learning with step-by-step guidance. Each exercise builds on the previous. All concepts from the session are coded. Banking/finance examples used for context.

objectives: Create, traverse, sort, search, and analyze arrays. Use the Arrays utility class. Practice both traditional for loops and enhanced for-each loops.
prerequisites: IntelliJ IDEA (Community Edition) or VS Code with Java Extension
Git installed and GitHub account created

exercises.title: Arrays — Branch Performance Dashboard
exercises.objective: Create, traverse, sort, search, and analyze arrays. Use the Arrays utility class. Practice both traditional for loops and enhanced for-each loops.
exercises.scenario: RoboBank has 6 branches across India. Build a performance dashboard that analyzes deposit amounts, sorts branches, finds top/bottom performers, and generates a formatted report.
instructions: Step 2: Implement all sections — each section teaches a new array concept
Step 4: MODIFICATION — Add a 7th branch 'Pune' with ₹95,00,000. Update the array. Do you need to change anything else?
Step 5: CHALLENGE at the end — implement without using Arrays.sort()

hints: Always initialize max/min to the first element (deposits[0]), NOT to 0. If all values were negative, 0 would incorrectly be the 'max'.
Arrays.copyOf() creates a new array with the same elements — so sorting the copy doesn't affect the original array and its index relationship with the branches array.
System.out.printf with %,.2f adds comma separators and 2 decimal places. The 'n' after the % is the flag for thousand separator (locale-specific).
reflection_questions: Why do we initialize maxDeposit = deposits[0] instead of maxDeposit = 0? When would maxDeposit = 0 give a wrong answer?
Why must we use Arrays.copyOf() before sorting if we want to find the branch name later?
Without Arrays.toString(), what does System.out.println(deposits) print? Try it — understand why the output looks strange.
exercises.debugging_task: Add this code: double[] emptyArr = new double[0]; System.out.println(emptyArr[0]); — what exception do you get? How would you safely handle an empty array before finding max/min?
